documents.title: H&P - Admission, Sepsis of Unclear Source
lines: HPI:
82 yo male brought to ED overnight by daughter for fever and acute confusion since the prior evening.
Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
No reported cough, dysuria, abdominal pain, or diarrhea per daughter. No recent travel. No falls.
Last seen at baseline 18:00 yesterday per family. Poor oral intake x 1 day.
ED Course:
Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Respiratory rate 22; SpO2 95% on RA, no oxygen needed.
Triage HR 118, BP 92/54.
Lactate 2.1 mmol/L at 02:10, not repeated. Vitals at 04:45 after fluids: HR 102, BP 104/62, RR 20.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Source unclear; blood culture x2 drawn at 02:20; urinalysis pending.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 04:30 as the only antibiotic dose.
Past Medical History:
HTN, paroxysmal AF (not on anticoagulation per pt preference), BPH, osteoarthritis, remote cholecystectomy.
No known CKD, baseline creatinine 0.9 mg/dL from prior outpatient labs.
Home Medications:
Amlodipine 5 mg daily
Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 500 mg PRN
Allergies: penicillin - rash in childhood, tolerated cephalosporins previously.
Social: lives alone in single-level home, daughter visits daily, ambulates without device. No tobacco, rare alcohol.
ROS:
Positive for fever, chills, weakness, confusion. Negative for chest pain, vomiting, hematuria, rash.
Physical Exam:
Gen: elderly male, ill-appearing, dry mucous membranes.
Neuro: awake, oriented to self only, follows simple commands, no focal deficit, no neck rigidity.
CV: tachycardic, irregular, no murmur, cap refill 3 sec.
Pulm: clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles, unlabored on room air.
Abd: soft, nondistended, no RUQ or suprapubic tenderness, no CVA tenderness.
Skin: warm, no cellulitis, no decubitus, no line sites.
GU: no scrotal swelling, no purulent urethral discharge.
MSK: no joint effusion or warmth.
Labs:
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 133, K 4.2, HCO3 19, BUN 42, glucose 138.
AST 38, ALT 30, T bili 1.1, INR 1.2.
CXR: no consolidation or effusion.
Assessment/Plan:
82 yo male with sepsis, source not yet identified, with AKI, mild thrombocytopenia, and encephalopathy.
1. Sepsis - continue empiric coverage, follow culture data, trend fever curve and WBC.
2. AKI - hold amlodipine, avoid NSAIDs, monitor urine output hourly, further fluids as tolerated by exam.
3. Thrombocytopenia - likely sepsis related, repeat CBC in AM, no transfusion indicated.
4. Encephalopathy - delirium precautions, frequent reorientation, avoid sedatives, monitor GCS q4h.
5. Source workup - urinalysis and urine culture, repeat exam of skin and abdomen in AM.
6. Rate control - continue metoprolol if BP tolerates.
Admit to stepdown telemetry. Attending notified at 05:05. Daughter updated at bedside.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: Subjective:
Pt slept several hours overnight. This morning states his own name and reports he is in the hospital. Denies pain, denies dysuria.
No fever since 06:00. Took full breakfast tray with encouragement.
Overnight Events:
Urine output 620 mL since admission. No further fluid boluses required after initial resuscitation.
Vitals 07:30: T 37.1 C, HR 88, BP 112/68, RR 18, SpO2 96% on RA.
Exam:
Gen: alert, more interactive, oriented to self, place, and year.
Neuro: GCS 15, no asterixis, moves all extremities.
CV: regular rate, no murmur. Pulm: clear. Abd: soft, nontender. No rash.
Labs:
WBC 13,400, bands not repeated. Platelets 121,000. Creatinine 1.6 mg/dL, HCO3 23.
Source unclear; blood culture x2 drawn at 02:20; urinalysis pending.
Assessment/Plan:
Sepsis, improving clinically with resolution of fever, tachycardia, and encephalopathy.
1. Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 04:30 as the only antibiotic dose; transitioned to oral cephalexin the next morning.
2. AKI - creatinine trending down, continue PO intake, recheck BMP later today, amlodipine still held.
3. Thrombocytopenia - improving, no bleeding, no further intervention.
4. Delirium resolved - mobilize with RN, out of bed to chair.
5. Discharge planning - if afternoon labs stable and pt remains afebrile, likely discharge home with daughter today.
Attending rounded at bedside 08:40, agrees with plan.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Afternoon
lines: Subjective:
Pt ambulated 40 feet in hallway with RN, no dizziness. Tolerating PO cephalexin without nausea.
Denies fever, chills, cough, or urinary symptoms. Wants to go home today.
Vitals:
No oxygen requirement at any point this admission.
Exam:
Alert, fully oriented, conversational and appropriate. Mucous membranes moist.
CV regular, lungs clear, abdomen benign, no skin findings, calves nontender.
Labs this afternoon:
Creatinine 1.3 mg/dL, K 4.0, BUN 24. Platelets 138,000. WBC 10,900.
Blood cultures no growth to date at 12 hours. Urinalysis negative for pyuria or nitrites, urine culture pending.
Assessment/Plan:
Sepsis, source remains unidentified, clinically resolved. Fever curve flat >12 h, hemodynamics normal off fluids.
1. Continue oral cephalexin to complete empiric course; pt counseled on penicillin allergy history and cephalosporin tolerance.
2. AKI resolving - restart amlodipine at follow-up only if BP elevated; keep held at discharge.
3. Platelets recovering, no further CBC needed inpatient.
4. Cultures to be followed after discharge; daughter given callback instructions.
5. Discharge home this afternoon with daughter, PCP follow up in 3 days for repeat BMP and culture review.
Discussed with attending 15:20, cleared for discharge.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD2
lines: Admit HD1, discharged HD2.
Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Sepsis, source unidentified, resolved
2. Acute kidney injury, resolving
3. Thrombocytopenia, resolved
4. Acute encephalopathy/delirium, resolved
5. Hypertension, paroxysmal atrial fibrillation, BPH
Hospital Course:
82 yo male presented overnight with fever and acute confusion. Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
Respiratory rate 22; SpO2 95% on RA, no oxygen needed.
Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Lactate 2.1 mmol/L at 02:10, not repeated. Vitals at 04:45 after fluids: HR 102, BP 104/62, RR 20.
Received 2.5 L normal saline bolus (30 mL/kg); BP after bolus 86/48, MAP 61.
Source unclear; blood culture x2 drawn at 02:20; urinalysis pending.
Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Ceftriaxone 1 g IV given at 04:30 as the only antibiotic dose; transitioned to oral cephalexin the next morning.
No vasopressors required. No ICU transfer. Afebrile from 06:00 HD2 onward.
By HD2 afternoon: WBC 10,900, platelets 138,000, creatinine 1.3 mg/dL. Blood cultures no growth at 12 h, urinalysis without pyuria, urine culture pending.
Mental status returned to baseline, ambulating independently in hallway.
Discharge Vitals:
Discharge Medications:
Cephalexin 500 mg PO q8h to complete empiric course
Metoprolol succinate 25 mg daily
Tamsulosin 0.4 mg nightly
Acetaminophen 500 mg PRN fever or pain
Amlodipine HELD at discharge given recent AKI
Follow Up:
PCP in 3 days for repeat BMP and review of pending blood and urine cultures.
Return precautions reviewed with pt and daughter: fever, confusion, decreased urine output, lightheadedness, poor PO intake.
Discharged home with daughter, ambulatory, no home services required.
